<issue identifier="MM-476">
<title>Brass Console: render the blob-integrity readout and did:web hosting flag</title>
<description>
<issue id="e95731ec-2922-4ebe-9ec4-27c836063e28" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-474/blob-observability-ownership-loss-is-indistinguishable-from-byte-loss">MM-474</issue> (PR #441) added three operator readouts to the API. None of them are rendered by the admin-companion app yet, so they are JSON an operator has to curl for — which is most of the gap <issue id="e95731ec-2922-4ebe-9ec4-27c836063e28" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-474/blob-observability-ownership-loss-is-indistinguishable-from-byte-loss">MM-474</issue> set out to close.

Same shape as the <issue id="6a22b24b-7904-49cc-b5dd-e4d5386b8b54" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-472/blob-gc-destroys-the-blobs-of-any-account-whose-reconcile-fails">MM-472</issue> → #439 split: the relay-side signal landed first, the console-side rendering followed separately.

## The fields

| Endpoint | Fields | What they mean |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /v1/admin/health` | `storage.blobUnownedCount`, `storage.blobUnownedBytes` | Stored blobs no account claims. Expect ~0 — GC drops a physical row with its last owner, so a row is unowned only between two statements. A standing value means bytes intact, ownership gone. |
| `GET /v1/accounts/:id/storage` | `uploadedBlobCount`, `uploadedBlobBytes` | Physical rows naming this account as uploader, beside the ownership figures. |
| `GET /v1/admin/accounts` | `didWebHosting` | Whether Custos serves this account's did:web document. |

## Suggested scope

1. **Status screen** — surface `blobUnownedCount`/`Bytes` in the storage block. This one is genuinely alertable: it needs no threshold tuning (~0 is the real baseline), and unlike a stale `blobGc.completedAt` it fires while the sweep is still running on schedule — the exact condition that made the original loss invisible for six hours. Worth a distinct treatment from the ordinary blob counts, not another neutral row.
2. **Account detail / storage** — show the uploaded figures beside the owned ones. Divergence here is **not** a fault by itself: blobs are content-addressed and shared, so owned-not-uploaded and uploaded-not-owned both occur normally. Present it as a second reading, not a warning — a red badge on benign sharing would train the operator to ignore it.
3. **Account list/detail** — a `didWebHosting` indicator. The flag gates a serve path that 404s indistinguishably from an unknown host when off, so its value is telling "not hosted" apart from "broken".

## Constraints

* Brass Console brief: `apps/admin-companion/PRODUCT.md` + `DESIGN.md` (terminal-native, cool-slate/gold, monospace-forward — **not** the Obsign register). Target `/impeccable` at `apps/admin-companion` so it loads the right brief.
* Status never by colour alone (WCAG 2.2 AAA): pair any integrity state with text + icon + position, the way the sweep rows already name `failed <n>` versus `stale`.
* Older relays predating these fields must degrade to "not reported" rather than failing the screen — the same posture #439 took for the sweep `errors` field.
</description>

</issue-relations>
</issue>

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jacob.zweifel/.claude/skills/linear-workflow

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

{"id":"MM-476","title":"Brass Console: render the blob-integrity readout and did:web hosting flag","description":"<issue id="e95731ec-2922-4ebe-9ec4-27c836063e28" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-474/blob-observability-ownership-loss-is-indistinguishable-from-byte-loss">MM-474</issue> (PR #441) added three operator readouts to the API. None of them are rendered by the admin-companion app yet, so they are JSON an operator has to curl for — which is most of the gap <issue id="e95731ec-2922-4ebe-9ec4-27c836063e28" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-474/blob-observability-ownership-loss-is-indistinguishable-from-byte-loss">MM-474</issue> set out to close.

Same shape as the <issue id="6a22b24b-7904-49cc-b5dd-e4d5386b8b54" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-472/blob-gc-destroys-the-blobs-of-any-account-whose-reconcile-fails">MM-472</issue> → #439 split: the relay-side signal landed first, the console-side rendering followed separately.

## The fields

| Endpoint | Fields | What they mean |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /v1/admin/health` | `storage.blobUnownedCount`, `storage.blobUnownedBytes` | Stored blobs no account claims. Expect ~0 — GC drops a physical row with its last owner, so a row is unowned only between two statements. A standing value means bytes intact, ownership gone. |
| `GET /v1/accounts/:id/storage` | `uploadedBlobCount`, `uploadedBlobBytes` | Physical rows naming this account as uploader, beside the ownership figures. |
| `GET /v1/admin/accounts` | `didWebHosting` | Whether Custos serves this account's did:web document. |

## Suggested scope

1. **Status screen** — surface `blobUnownedCount`/`Bytes` in the storage block. This one is genuinely alertable: it needs no threshold tuning (~0 is the real baseline), and unlike a stale `blobGc.completedAt` it fires while the sweep is still running on schedule — the exact condition that made the original loss invisible for six hours. Worth a distinct treatment from the ordinary blob counts, not another neutral row.
2. **Account detail / storage** — show the uploaded figures beside the owned ones. Divergence here is **not** a fault by itself: blobs are content-addressed and shared, so owned-not-uploaded and uploaded-not-owned both occur normally. Present it as a second reading, not a warning — a red badge on benign sharing would train the operator to ignore it.
3. **Account list/detail** — a `didWebHosting` indicator. The flag gates a serve path that 404s indistinguishably from an unknown host when off, so its value is telling "not hosted" apart from "broken".

## Constraints

* Brass Console brief: `apps/admin-companion/PRODUCT.md` + `DESIGN.md` (terminal-native, cool-slate/gold, monospace-forward — **not** the Obsign register). Target `/impeccable` at `apps/admin-companion` so it loads the right brief.
* Status never by colour alone (WCAG 2.2 AAA): pair any integrity state with text + icon + position, the way the sweep rows already name `failed <n>` versus `stale`.

content.content: @AGENTS.md

# Admin Companion (operator console) Mobile App

Last verified: 2026-07-10
Last updated: 2026-07-25 (Status screen surfaces each sweep's `errors` count as a named `failed <n>` fault, distinct from `stale`)

## Purpose

Tauri v2 iOS app — SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 frontend in a WKWebView over a Rust
backend, communicating through Tauri IPC. The operator-facing console for an ezpds
relay: generate/share account claim codes, pair admin devices via QR, and revoke
devices. A **separate product** from identity-wallet (Obsign) with its own
terminal-native design register — see [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md) / [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md)
and the design plan [docs/archive/design-plans/2026-06-26-admin-companion-app.md](../../docs/archive/design-plans/2026-06-26-admin-companion-app.md).

The relay side (pairing/auth/device endpoints, Phases 1–5) is already shipped. This
app is built across Phases 6–8.

## Browser test harness (drive the app without a simulator)

The whole frontend runs in a plain desktop browser under `vite dev`; the harness
intercepts the Tauri `invoke()` seam with the official `mockIPC` so an agent can reach
every operator screen and reproduce any state without a Mac/Xcode/simulator. Mirrors the
identity-wallet harness exactly (same `window.__harness` API shape). Design + acceptance
criteria: [docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md](../../docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md).

**Start it** (or use the `.claude/launch.json` config `admin-harness` / `admin-harness-proxy`):
- **Fake mode** (default, no backend): `pnpm --dir apps/admin-companion dev:harness` → http://localhost:5174.
- **Proxy mode** (real signed operator requests against a hermetic local PDS): `cargo build -p pds`,
  then `just harness-pds` (prints URL + admin token), then
  `VITE_HARNESS_PDS_URL=<url> VITE_HARNESS_ADMIN_TOKEN=<token> pnpm --dir apps/admin-companion dev:harness:proxy`.
  Proxy mode starts **unpaired** by default — pair for real from the Pair screen (the
  harness mints the pairing code via the admin API and self-signs the registration).
- Plain `pnpm dev` never activates the harness (double-gated on `import.meta.env.DEV && VITE_HARNESS`);
  `pnpm check:harness-absence` proves it is tree-shaken out of production builds.

**`window.__harness` console API:** `.scenario(name)` (presets: `unpaired`, `single-relay`,
`multi-relay`, `degraded-health`, `flagged-accounts`; `.scenarios` lists them), `.failNext(command, error)`
(e.g. `window.__harness.failNext('generate_claim_code', { code: 'NOT_PAIRED' })`),
`.emit(event, payload)` (kept for parity — this app subscribes to no Tauri events),
`.state()` (read-only snapshot), `.mode`.

**Biometric gate:** the plugin is allowed to resolve in the browser (`plugin:biometric|authenticate`),
so signing actions proceed. To exercise the disabled path, set it off via the Settings
toggle / `set_biometric_enabled(false)` (outcome `skipped`); to force a denial, use
`window.__harness.failNext('plugin:biometric|authenticate', {})`. Do **not** try to drive
QR-scan pairing in the browser — barcode scanning is out of scope; use the Pair screen's
manual-entry fields (fake) or auto-mint (proxy).

**Proxy mode is real for the signed-request surface** — `pair_device`, `generate_claim_code`,
and `list_admin_devices` sign the canonical envelopes (`src/lib/harness/proxy/signing.ts`,
byte-for-byte the Rust `signing.rs`) with a real WebCrypto P-256 key, and the relay's
`require_admin` accepts them. Every other command falls through to the fake.

**Fake handler coverage is enforced:** every command in `$lib/ipc.ts` must have a handler in
`src/lib/harness/registry.ts` or `registry.test.ts` fails. Harness code lives in
`src/lib/harness/`, activated by `src/hooks.client.ts`.

## Contracts

### Rust backend (`src-tauri/`)
- `device_key::get_or_create() -> Result<DevicePublicKey, DeviceKeyError>` — idempotent;
  returns `{ multibase, keyId }` (camelCase for IPC). Same crypto as identity-wallet's
  module; here the key is the device's **admin credential** (signs requests), not a
  did:plc rotation key.
- `device_key::sign(data) -> Result<Vec<u8>, DeviceKeyError>` — raw 64-byte (r‖s),
  **low-S normalized** P-256 signature (the relay's verifier rejects high-S).
- `DeviceKeyError` / `RelayClientError` serialize as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE", … }`.
  The biometric-pref IPC commands surface keychain errors through `RelayClientError::Keychain`
  (the app's single Serialize error type) rather than exposing `KeychainError` directly.
- Keychain accounts: device-key accounts unchanged (`admin-device-key-priv`, `admin-device-key-pub` +
  `admin-device-key-app-label`); `admin-pairings` (the versioned multi-relay document, replaces the
  legacy triple); `admin-biometric-enabled` (the gate preference, unchanged). Removal semantics:
  a sole remaining pairing is always auto-promoted to active (unambiguous — even when the selection
  was already cleared by an earlier ambiguous removal); removing the active pairing with two or
  more remaining clears the selection and the UI must ask for an explicit pick (never silent
  relay switch). A corrupt document (parse error, version mismatch, invalid active reference) is a
  hard error surfaced as `RelayClientError::Keychain` — never a silent reset, which would be
  indistinguishable from a successful unpair. Removing a pairing returns the `NO_SUCH_PAIRING` error
  code when the id does not exist. "Unpair" is local-only (removes a pairing document entry) and keeps
  the device key (so a re-pair is recognised by the same public key) and keeps `admin-biometric-enabled`
  (a device setting, not pairing state).
- **Signing contract is single-source-of-truth and must stay in lockstep with the relay.**
  `signing.rs`'s golden tests pin the exact literals the relay's `auth.rs` tests pin; if the
  relay changes an envelope, both tests break together. Signatures are low-S P-256, raw r‖s,
  base64url-no-pad; the body field is `sha256_hex(exact_request_bytes)`. The client serializes
  a request body **once** and signs+sends those same bytes so the relay's recomputed hash matches.

### Frontend

- `src/lib/ipc.ts` is the **only** file that calls `invoke()`; pages import from it. Pure
  parsers that carry no IPC (e.g. `parsePairingPayload`) live in their own modules, not `ipc.ts`.
- **Shared route helpers** factor out the three copy-paste patterns the per-server operator
  screens repeated. The security-relevant "pin the pairing at entry so a concurrent active
  switch can't redirect what a screen reads or signs" logic lives once:
  - `src/lib/pinned-pairing.ts` (Functional Core) — `resolvePinnedPairing(state, searchParams)`
    (pin from `?server=`, else the active pairing), `loadPinnedPairing(searchParams)` (the
    `onMount` load + resolve), and `pinnedHref(path, pairingId, extra?)` (uniform `?server=…`
    link construction). Rendered by `components/ui/PinnedPairingGate.svelte`, which shows the
    three pre-flight states (checking / check-failed / no-server) and hands the resolved,
    non-null pairing to its `children` snippet. Used by Devices, Codes, Accounts, Account
    detail, Moderation, Status, Transfers.
  - `src/lib/guarded-action.svelte.ts` — `createGuardedActions()`: a reactive controller owning
    the per-row busy/error maps + one gate-hint line for a biometric-gated relay action (busy
    flag claimed synchronously before the gate await; a denial is a quiet hint). Used by
    Devices/Codes/Transfers. (Settings keeps its own revoke logic — it shares one gate hint with
    the non-gated local-forget and reloads on error, a different shape.)
  - `src/lib/paged-list.svelte.ts` — `createPagedList(fetchPage)`: a reactive controller for a
    cursor-paged relay list (loading/error/ready-with-cursor + a separate paging-error slot so a
    failed page keeps the shown rows). Used by Codes/Transfers. (Accounts keeps its own
    generation-counter pagination — it layers search + filter re-fetches on top.)
  - `src/lib/armed-action.svelte.ts` — `createArmedAction()`: a reactive controller for an armed
    two-tap + biometric-gated destructive action (arm → confirm → gate → run, with an optional
    `commit` guard so a slow write can't land under a newer lookup). Moderation runs two
    independent instances (takedown + credential sweep), each treating the other's `writing` as a
    lock so two prompts never stack.
- SSR/prerender disabled globally (`src/routes/+layout.ts`); static SPA in `dist/`.
- **Pairing QR payload** is JSON `{"relayUrl","pairingCode"}` (parsed by
  `parsePairingPayload` in `src/lib/pairing-payload.ts`); the operator's code-minting tool encodes
  it. Manual entry fills the same two fields, so pairing works on the simulator (no camera).
- **Mobile-only plugins** (camera QR, biometric, share) follow one pattern: the Rust dep is
  `cfg(target_os ios/android)`-gated in `Cargo.toml`, registered behind `#[cfg(mobile)]` in
  `lib.rs`, granted in `src-tauri/capabilities/mobile.json` (`platforms: [iOS, android]`), and
  imported **dynamically** in JS so the host/desktop build never resolves it. The host build
  skips the mobile capability, so `cargo build/test -p admin-companion` stays Apple-toolchain-free.

    called before every signing action (claim code, self-revoke). Needs `NSFaceIDUsageDescription`.

    `allowDeviceCredential`) — it never pre-skips on `checkStatus().isAvailable`, which is false on a
    passcode-only device even though the passcode could still gate authentication. The gate resolves to allow only when the

```bash
nix develop --impure --accept-flake-config   # from workspace ROOT
cd apps/admin-companion && pnpm install
cargo tauri ios init                          # generates gitignored src-tauri/gen/ (renders scripts/ios/project.yml)
cd ../.. && just admin-postinit               # swift-rs check + app icon + verify (idempotent)
just admin-dev                                # simulator   (or: just admin-build)
```

Host build / tests (no Xcode): `cargo build -p admin-companion`, `cargo test -p admin-companion`.

## Key decisions

- **Toolchain scripts are SHARED, design is forked.** The iOS toolchain scripts
  (`scripts/ios-env.sh`, `ios-postinit.sh`, `ios-check.sh`) are thin wrappers over the
  single shared implementation in the repo-root `scripts/ios/` (each wrapper pins this
  app's dir and the `admin` recipe prefix), and the Xcode-project workarounds come from
  the SHARED XcodeGen template `scripts/ios/project.yml` (rendered on every
  `cargo tauri ios init` via `bundle > iOS > template`), so neither the script logic nor
  the project workarounds can diverge between the two app lanes. This app's framework
  list lives in its `tauri.conf.json` `bundle > iOS > frameworks` — just
  `SystemConfiguration`; no AuthenticationServices, this app has no in-app OAuth
  plugin. The
  OKLCH token *architecture* is forked from identity-wallet — but the token *values*,
  components, and product/design briefs are this app's own terminal-native register.
  See the root `apps/identity-wallet/AGENTS.md` for the full explanation of every iOS
  patch and the toolchain seam; it is the single source of truth for those gotchas
  (this app reuses the same swift-rs `[patch.crates-io]`).

  Apple `security-framework` toolchain. Built/checked on macOS via `just admin-*`.
- **Grotesk UI font is provisional** (system SF Pro via `--font-sans`) until the
  `/impeccable` font pass; JetBrains Mono (the signature voice) is bundled in `static/fonts/`.
- **App icon: `app-icon.svg` is the source of truth** (brand rationale in DESIGN.md §6);
  `app-icon.png` is its 1024×1024 render and the input `cargo tauri icon` consumes.
  `just admin-postinit` regenerates the gitignored AppIcon asset catalog from
  it after every `cargo tauri ios init` (desktop/android outputs go to the gitignored
  `src-tauri/icons-build/`), and `just admin-check` verifies the catalog was built from
  the current PNG via a sha256 marker. To change the icon: edit the SVG, re-render the
  PNG at 1024×1024 (e.g. resvg), commit both, re-run `just admin-postinit`.
  **`AppIcon.icon/` is the layered Icon Composer document** (icon.json + `Assets/*.svg`
  layers split from the same master — no baked shadows; Liquid Glass supplies lighting):
  the XcodeGen template (`scripts/ios/project.yml`) references it in place as a resource
  so Xcode 26 renders the layered iOS 26 icon (the flat appiconset stays as the
  older-toolchain fallback), and `just admin-pr-check` compiles it with actool
  (`just _icon-compile`) so a bad icon.json fails the PR gate. Keep the layer geometry
  in sync with `app-icon.svg`.
- **Distinct Keychain namespace** (`"ezpds-admin-companion"`) and bundle id
  (`dev.malpercio.admincompanion`) so the two apps never collide on one device.

content.text:
Full picture in hand. Here's the key design judgment before I write code:

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The sweep-`errors` precedent defaulted a missing field to `0`, which was safe because 0 there means "no failures". For `blobUnownedCount`, **0 is the healthy baseline** — so defaulting an absent field to 0 would fabricate an all-clear from an old relay. These three fields must be `Option`/nullable so "not reported" stays distinguishable from "reported as zero".
- Serde gives that for free: a missing field on an `Option<T>` deserializes to `None` without `#[serde(default)]`. The existing `#[serde(default)]` attributes on `flags`/`errors` are there precisely because `Vec`/`i64` have no such rule.
- The verdict/fact split in this app is load-bearing: `health.ts` holds judgment (thresholds, alarms), `format.ts` holds verdict-free rendering. The unowned pair carries an alarm, so it goes in `health.ts`; uploaded figures and the hosting flag are facts, so they go in `format.ts`.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
Now the Rust wire structs.

content.thinking:
The `.dd--alarm` class isn't being applied even though `ddColor` matches the plain dd color — I'm checking if Svelte's scoped CSS is the culprit, but `svelte-check` shows no warnings. Looking at the actual issue: `querySelector('.dd--alarm')` is finding the element, so the dd exists and `ddColor` isn't null, which means something else is preventing the styling from taking effect.

Ah, it's a specificity problem — `.facts dd` (0,1,1) beats `.dd--alarm` (0,1,0). I need to increase the specificity by targeting `.facts dd.dd--alarm` instead. The text content still conveys the meaning ("ownership lost !") thanks to the AAA design principle, but the visual emphasis I intended is missing without the color change.

content.text:
The visual check caught a real bug: my alarm color was silently losing a CSS specificity contest.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
`.dd--alarm` (specificity 0,1,0) loses to the existing `.facts dd` (0,1,1), so the alarm row rendered in the plain muted ink. Notably the *meaning* still survived — the value itself says `ownership lost !` — which is the AAA "never color alone" rule paying off: the bug cost emphasis, not information.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Brass Console: render the blob-integrity readouts and did:web hosting flag

The relay already reported three operator readouts; none were rendered by the
console, so they were JSON an operator had to curl for.

- Status → Storage now names unowned blobs (stored rows no account claims). It
  is the one alertable figure on the screen and the only one carrying a verdict,
  so it gets its own row plus a stated consequence, not another neutral line. It
  needs no threshold — collection drops a physical row with its last owner, so
  ~0 is the real baseline — and is strictly more sensitive than the blob GC sweep
  line beside it, which can only report a sweep that stopped.
- Account detail shows an account's uploaded blob figures beside its owned ones.
  Deliberately verdict-free: blobs are shared, so divergence is benign in both
  directions, and a badge on it would teach the operator to ignore badges.
- The account row states did:web hosting, and only for did:web accounts — the
  question does not arise for did:plc, and answering it everywhere would bury
  the rows where the answer means something.

All three degrade to "not reported" on an older relay. They are modelled as
nullable rather than defaulted — the opposite choice from the sweep `errors`
field — because for each of them the zero/false value is itself a meaningful
reading, so defaulting would fabricate an all-clear the relay never gave.

Verified live in the browser harness across the healthy and degraded scenarios.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && gh pr create --base main --title "Brass Console: render the blob-integrity readouts and did:web hosting flag (MM-476)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Closes [MM-476](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-476/brass-console-render-the-blob-integrity-readout-and-didweb-hosting).

MM-474 (#441) added three operator readouts to the API. None were rendered by the admin-companion app, so they were JSON an operator had to curl for — which was most of the gap MM-474 set out to close. Same shape as the MM-472 → #439 split: relay-side signal first, console-side rendering separately.

## What each one does

**Status → Storage: `unowned blobs`.** Stored blob rows no account claims. This is the one genuinely alertable figure on the screen and the only one carrying a verdict, so it does not sit in the neutral run of counts — it gets its own named row plus, when a population is actually reported, a stated consequence beneath the grid. It needs no threshold tuning (collection drops a physical row together with its last owner, so ~0 is the real baseline), and it is strictly more sensitive than the `blob GC` sweep line beside it: staleness can only report a sweep that *stopped*, while this fires with the sweep running exactly on schedule — the condition that once kept a real loss invisible for six hours.

**Account detail: `uploaded blobs`.** The physical rows naming the account as first uploader, beside the ownership figures the rest of the panel reports. Deliberately verdict-free and unmarked, with a note saying why: blobs are content-addressed and shared, so owned-not-uploaded and uploaded-not-owned both occur normally, and a badge on that benign divergence would train the operator to ignore badges.

**Account row: did:web hosting.** `served here` / `not served here` / `not reported`, in the same muted register as the quota readout — hosting off is a configuration, not a fault. Rendered **only** for did:web accounts: the question does not arise for did:plc (whose document lives on plc.directory), and answering it on every row would bury the rows where the answer means something.

## The degradation choice worth reviewing

All three degrade to `not reported` on an older relay, per the posture #439 took for the sweep `errors` field — but by a **different mechanism**, and that difference is the main design decision here.

`errors` could safely `serde(default)` a missing value to `0`, because 0 there means "no failures". For these three, the zero/false value is itself a meaningful reading — `blobUnownedCount: 0` is precisely this readout's all-clear — so defaulting would fabricate an all-clear an older relay never gave. They are therefore modelled as `Option`/nullable end-to-end, and the three outcomes (`not reported` / `none` / a marked line) are never collapsed. Serde maps a missing field to `None` on an `Option` without an attribute; the Rust deserialization tests pin that, including the older-relay JSON.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p admin-companion` — 90 passed; `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean.
- `pnpm test` — 195 passed (19 files), including new unit tests for `unownedBlobLine`, `uploadedBlobsLine`, and `didWebHostingLine` covering all three degradation outcomes and the never-color-alone contract.
- `pnpm check` — 0 errors. It caught a real bug: an `AccountListEntry` literal in `flags.test.ts` missing the new required field.
- Driven live in the browser harness across the `single-relay` and `degraded-health` scenarios. That caught a second real bug — the alarm row's `.dd--alarm` rule (specificity 0,1,0) was losing to the existing `.facts dd` rule (0,1,1) and rendering in plain ink. Worth noting that the *meaning* survived anyway, because the value itself reads `ownership lost !` — the AAA "never by colour alone" rule doing its job.
- Harness fixtures seed a reported zero when healthy and a standing population when degraded, plus one did:web account per relay, so all three states are reachable without a simulator. `/preview` gains the three hosting readings.
- `just ticket-ref-check`, `changelog-check`, `docs-check`, `check:harness-absence` all pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

{"id":"MM-476","title":"Brass Console: render the blob-integrity readout and did:web hosting flag","description":"<issue id="e95731ec-2922-4ebe-9ec4-27c836063e28" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-474/blob-observability-ownership-loss-is-indistinguishable-from-byte-loss">MM-474</issue> (PR #441) added three operator readouts to the API. None of them are rendered by the admin-companion app yet, so they are JSON an operator has to curl for — which is most of the gap <issue id="e95731ec-2922-4ebe-9ec4-27c836063e28" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-474/blob-observability-ownership-loss-is-indistinguishable-from-byte-loss">MM-474</issue> set out to close.

Same shape as the <issue id="6a22b24b-7904-49cc-b5dd-e4d5386b8b54" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-472/blob-gc-destroys-the-blobs-of-any-account-whose-reconcile-fails">MM-472</issue> → #439 split: the relay-side signal landed first, the console-side rendering followed separately.

## The fields

| Endpoint | Fields | What they mean |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /v1/admin/health` | `storage.blobUnownedCount`, `storage.blobUnownedBytes` | Stored blobs no account claims. Expect ~0 — GC drops a physical row with its last owner, so a row is unowned only between two statements. A standing value means bytes intact, ownership gone. |
| `GET /v1/accounts/:id/storage` | `uploadedBlobCount`, `uploadedBlobBytes` | Physical rows naming this account as uploader, beside the ownership figures. |
| `GET /v1/admin/accounts` | `didWebHosting` | Whether Custos serves this account's did:web document. |

## Suggested scope

1. **Status screen** — surface `blobUnownedCount`/`Bytes` in the storage block. This one is genuinely alertable: it needs no threshold tuning (~0 is the real baseline), and unlike a stale `blobGc.completedAt` it fires while the sweep is still running on schedule — the exact condition that made the original loss invisible for six hours. Worth a distinct treatment from the ordinary blob counts, not another neutral row.
2. **Account detail / storage** — show the uploaded figures beside the owned ones. Divergence here is **not** a fault by itself: blobs are content-addressed and shared, so owned-not-uploaded and uploaded-not-owned both occur normally. Present it as a second reading, not a warning — a red badge on benign sharing would train the operator to ignore it.
3. **Account list/detail** — a `didWebHosting` indicator. The flag gates a serve path that 404s indistinguishably from an unknown host when off, so its value is telling "not hosted" apart from "broken".

## Constraints

* Brass Console brief: `apps/admin-companion/PRODUCT.md` + `DESIGN.md` (terminal-native, cool-slate/gold, monospace-forward — **not** the Obsign register). Target `/impeccable` at `apps/admin-companion` so it loads the right brief.
* Status never by colour alone (WCAG 2.2 AAA): pair any integrity state with text + icon + position, the way the sweep rows already name `failed <n>` versus `stale`.

content.text:
Done. [PR #452](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/452) is open; MM-476 is In Review with the PR attached.

## What shipped

All three MM-474 readouts now render, each with the treatment the issue asked for:

- **Status → Storage** ([status/+page.svelte](apps/admin-companion/src/routes/status/+page.svelte)) names `unowned blobs` in its own row, with a stated consequence beneath the grid when a population is reported. Distinct from the neutral counts, as asked.
- **Account detail** ([account/+page.svelte](apps/admin-companion/src/routes/account/+page.svelte)) shows `uploaded blobs` beside the owned figures, verdict-free, with a note explaining why divergence is normal.
- **Account row** ([AccountRow.svelte](apps/admin-companion/src/lib/components/ui/AccountRow.svelte)) states did:web hosting — only on did:web rows.

## The judgment call worth your review

The degradation posture matches #439's *intent* but not its *mechanism*. `errors` could safely default a missing value to `0` because 0 there means "no failures". Here **0 is the all-clear** — `blobUnownedCount: 0` is exactly what a healthy server reports — so defaulting would fabricate an all-clear an old relay never gave. I modelled all three as `Option`/nullable end-to-end instead, keeping `not reported` / `none` / alarm as three distinct outcomes. If you'd rather they matched #439 literally, that's the line to push back on.

## Two real bugs the verification caught

Worth flagging because they argue for keeping both checks in the loop:

1. `pnpm check` found an `AccountListEntry` literal in `flags.test.ts` missing the new required field — the unit tests passed regardless, since vitest doesn't typecheck.
2. Driving the harness found my alarm-tone rule silently losing a CSS specificity contest (`.dd--alarm` at 0,1,0 vs the existing `.facts dd` at 0,1,1). The tests couldn't have caught it. Notably the *meaning* survived anyway — the value reads `ownership lost !` on its own — which is the never-colour-alone rule earning its keep.

Verification: 90 Rust tests, 195 frontend tests, clippy clean, `pnpm check` 0 errors, and both harness scenarios driven live. Harness fixtures seed the healthy zero, the degraded population, and a did:web account per relay, so all three states are reachable without a simulator.
